A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ScreenParse/ScreenVLM research, with complete, readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Pages 2–28 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; differences are confined to first-page metadata and typesetting.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on ScreenParse, GroundCUA, and ScreenSpot, including loss ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 3–7, appendix Table 9, and the qualitative figures.

M1.justification: The Webshot pipeline, ScreenTag representation, ScreenVLM architecture, and structure-aware training objective are identical, including their appendix specifications.

E1.justification: Both versions use ScreenParse for training and evaluation and retain GroundCUA and ScreenSpot Web/PC/Mobile evaluation. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same Qwen3-VL, InternVL3, OmniParser v2, YOLO, and RT-DETRv2 models and ScreenParse-trained variants in Tables 3–7 and 9.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, evaluation sample counts, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and inference procedures are unchanged in Section 5 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The loss ablation in Table 6, foundation-model fine-tuning analysis, efficiency comparison, training curves, and appendix qualitative case studies are retained without modification.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains latency reporting as mean plus or minus standard deviation over 128 samples. Neither version differs in seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including appendix results. For example, ScreenVLM retains PageIoU 0.606 on ScreenParse in Table 3 and 0.251 on GroundCUA in Table 4.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, weighted-loss equation, and mathematical metric definitions in Appendix 7.3 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about dense screen supervision, compact ScreenVLM parsing, and transfer to other models and benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of transfer and localization performance remain identical, as do the limitations concerning web-centric training, desktop/mobile domain gaps, and residual annotation noise.

D1.justification: Hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, pipeline specifications, and prompts are unchanged. The project-page link and Appendix 7.6 statement that Webshot code will be released also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to sparse grounding datasets and existing parsers are identical. The updated publication notice does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds Marc Pollefeys's Microsoft affiliation, replaces the preprint notice with ICML 2026 proceedings and copyright information, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Research prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author line, abstract placement, and affiliation/publication footnotes undergo slight reflow. All figures, tables, and layouts on pages 2–28 are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliation and publication information with slight first-page typesetting adjustments. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and complete appendix remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
